extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, and IP practitioners interested in GCC/regional patent protection and searching the GCC patent register/gazette
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive guidance on the Patent Office of the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf (GCC): scope of protection, filing acceptance rules, online register and gazette features, and search-related particulars. Useful for applicants, attorneys, and people performing patent searches or freedom-to-operate checks in the GCC region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of protection of GCC patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates of patents granted by the GCC Patent Office secure legal protection of the inventor's rights in all GCC Member States. A patent is validated in the Member States as of the date of grant in the GCC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A granted GCC patent confers regional protection across all member states (UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Kuwait) and takes effect as validated in each Member State from the GCC grant date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership and jurisdictional composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The GCC Patent Office is a regional office for the Gulf Cooperation Council, which comprises the United Arab Emirates, Kingdom of Bahrain, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Sultanate of Oman, State of Qatar, and State of Kuwait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know which states are covered by GCC patent protection when assessing territorial scope; this list defines the jurisdictional reach of GCC patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCC is not party to PCT or Paris Convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gulf Cooperation Council is neither a member of the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) nor of the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants cannot rely on PCT procedures or automatic Paris Convention country-level mechanisms via the GCC; check alternative national routes or priority claim practices applicable to GCC filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessation of new GCC filings after 6 January 2021
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the decision held by the 41st GCC Supreme Council meeting to amend the existing GCC Patent Law, no new filings were accepted by the GCC Patent Office for GCC patent applications after January 6, 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only patents filed before that date and subsequently granted retain the original regional validity; do not attempt to file new GCC regional patent applications after this cutoff unless using later provisions described (see resumed use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumption by national IP offices with limited validity
rubrics_metrics.description: IP Offices of Bahrain and Kuwait (since January 1, 2023) and Qatar (since July 1, 2023) have resumed the possibility to use the GCC Patent Office as IP authority; however, applications filed after the resuming date have a validity limited to the national territory of the filing country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the resumption dates, filings routed via GCC procedures by these national offices do not automatically get regional (all-member) effect — they are limited to the filing country's national territory. Confirm per-country transitional rules and dates when filing or evaluating rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term extension not available at GCC level
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection through Patent Term Extension is not available at the GCC level; referral is made to each country's national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patent term adjustments or extensions (e.g., regulatory data protection, SPC-like regimes), consult the relevant national IP/medicines legislation rather than expecting a regional GCC mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Patent Register: contents and search functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: The online patent register includes only granted patents and has an Arabic, English, French and Japanese interface. Through the patent register you can retrieve basic information on Legal Status (deduced from a code). The patent register can be searched by Applicant/Inventor Name, by Priority Data (by priority date only). There is also a previous release of the patent database providing information about the Legal Status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searchers should note the register covers granted patents only (not pending applications), supports multilingual interfaces, and has limited priority searching (by date only). Legal status is presented via codes — users must interpret codes (e.g., 'Expired'). Use the previous release link if needed for historical/legal-status details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Gazette: availability and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The online gazette is available in English with coverage from 2001 (issue no.1) to present (issues no.1-15 temporarily not available). Most documents are available in HTML and/or PDF format. Through the online gazette it is possible to access the Full Publications and lists of patents and applications granted, fallen or rejected and the archived releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Gazette to access full publications and chronological lists (granted, fallen, rejected). Be aware of temporary gaps in early issues and that materials are primarily in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Status reporting / search tip
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal Status in the register is reported via codes; an example of a status reported is 'Expired' for certain patent numbers (e.g., 2148).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting search results, translate legal-status codes to human-readable statuses (granted, expired, fallen, rejected). Example entries may help familiarize users with the register's coding conventions.
